messages:
maria: FYI we just got a DSAR erase request and the automated erasure pipeline errored out. looks like IAM bindings changed during last week's tidy-up and the eraser couldn't decrypt snapshots.
dan: can you paste the job error?
maria: from the eraser logs:

ERROR EraseRunner attempt=1 user=U-77421 status=FAILED reason=KMS.AccessDenied message=serviceAccount:eraser-prod@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com denied `cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt` for projects/redwood-kms/locations/global/keyRings/vec-keys/cryptoKeys/embeddings-key

maria: snapshot decryption step failed so the job marked as completed=false and left tombstones unverified.
kevin: i remember removing some old svcaccts. we rolled authz-cleanup PR #3540 that removed eraser-prod but intended to switch to ephemeral-runner. looks like the rollout missed this region.
sophie: legal perspective: if we can't cryptographically prove deletion, we must treat as not-deleted. preserve all evidence and do not respond to requester saying erased. also need a signed breakglass process if we temporarily re-enable rights.
privacy-bot: canonical runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/privacy/eraser-iam-failure. key points: do not mutate snapshots without documented approval; collect immutable evidence bundle; use timeboxed least-privilege when restoring access.
dan: ops-oncall can you check audit log for when binding was removed and whether key rotated?
ops-oncall: checking: IAM binding removed by org:authz-bot at 2025-10-02T02:11:09Z. KMS key embeddings-key shows primary version v4 active; v3 had binding for eraser. no rotation since then. i can re-enable the eraser svcacct and grant decrypt on the single key for 30 minutes if privacy+legal sign off.
maria: remediation options i see:
1) temporarily re-grant decrypt permission to eraser-prod for the specific key and run the purge, then immediately revoke. fastest but needs signed approvals and audit logging.
2) ask KMS team to rewrap affected snapshots to a key the ephemeral runner can access (requires ops + change control; slower).
3) restore the user's snapshot into a secure staging project where an oncall with breakglass can run manual verification and deletion with forensics watching.
kevin: prefer 1 for speed but must enforce least-privilege: IAM binding scoped to resource (single key) and time-limited. also log all commands and stdout to a sealed bucket.
sophie: legal: require an evidence bundle that includes: ticket id, who approved, IAM diff, KMS key version metadata, job run id, and checksums of deleted records. also require retention-exception if we delay beyond X days — i'll draft the approval template.
dan: tech followups:
- add preflight: try decrypt a known test envelope before starting erasure (fail-fast).
- change pipeline to mark FAILED_HOLD when KMS decrypt fails and stop automatic retries.
- emit verification hash after delete and store in sealed artifact.
ops-oncall: i'll prepare a small IAM delta export and Cloud Audit Logs snapshot. once legal provides signed doc we can do 30m window.
maria: opening ticket SR-2026-9902 and attaching logs + runbook. action list:
- maria: open ticket and attach logs/evidence (doing now).
- ops-oncall: stand by to enable svcacct + grant decrypt for one key for 30m on legal approval. export audit diff.
- kevin/dan: add preflight decrypt check and FAILED_HOLD state to pipeline. PR to follow.
- sophie: publish breakglass approval template and sign-off list.
privacy-bot: checklist items added to SR-2026-9902. link: https://redwood.internal/tickets/SR-2026-9902
maria: note if we can't get temporary rights quickly we need a retention-exception request so we don't inadvertently violate SLA claiming deletion. legal: what window is acceptable?
sophie: retention exception can be requested but expect a 24-72h turnaround for initial review depending on risk. for now preserve all artifacts and mark the requester response as "in progress".
kevin: follow-up: we'll add a small guard so that any KMS failure trips an escalation to privacy ops and does not mark the DSAR as done.
dan: sending :lock: :eyes: reaction. we'll keep this thread updated as approvals come in.
